passage:
After getting new glasses, Oliver realized the classroom board was not supposed to be blurry. Leaves on trees had clear edges, and street signs were easier to read.
He felt happy, but also embarrassed. He had thought he was bad at copying notes because he was slow. In fact, he simply could not see well.
His teacher moved him closer to the front until he got used to the glasses.
Oliver's grades improved, but more importantly, he stopped blaming himself.
He learned that sometimes people struggle not because they are lazy or careless, but because a problem has not been found yet. A clear view can change more than what the eyes see.
